concept_uz: Miloddan avvalgi VI asr, Kroton. Pifagor torni ikkiga boʻlib, musiqa sonlarga boʻysunishini topadi va «hamma narsa — son» deydi. Burilish: uning teoremasini bobilliklar ming yil oldin bilgan, uning oʻz isboti esa hech bir kasrga sigʻmaydigan uzunlikni — kvadrat diagonalini topib qoʻyadi.

facts.claim: Miloddan avvalgi VI asrda Janubiy Italiyadagi Kroton shahrida Samos orolidan kelgan Pifagor maktab ochgan; gʻoyasi «Hamma narsa — son»
Temirchi bolgʻalari haqidagi hikoya rivoyat, ehtimol toʻqilgan; lekin ortidagi kashfiyot haqiqiy
Torning yarmi — oʻsha nota, yuqoriroq (oktava, 2 : 1); 3 : 2 nisbat ham yoqimli uygʻunlik beradi

facts.claim: Bu qoidani bobilliklar Pifagordan ming yilcha oldin bilgan: taxminan m.a. 1800-yilga oid loy taxtachada mos sonlar ustunlari bor
Pifagorchilarning xizmati — qoidani isbotlashni muhim deb bilgani
Tomoni 1 boʻlgan kvadratning diagonali √2; uni hech qanday kasr bilan aniq yozib boʻlmaydi (irratsional son)

style_line: Cinematic photoreal historical drama, ancient Greek southern Italy in the 6th century BC, warm Mediterranean sunlight, white limestone, olive green and sea blue, soft haze, 35mm film look, quiet sense of wonder. No text, no letters, no numbers, no writing, no watermark.

refs.prompt: Vertical 9:16 wide shot of an ancient Greek seaside town in southern Italy around 530 BC: white limestone houses with terracotta roofs, a small temple with simple columns, olive trees, a stone courtyard, the deep blue sea behind under warm afternoon sun. No people.

Vertical 9:16 full-body portrait of a respectful reconstruction of the ancient Greek thinker Pythagoras, about 60: long white beard, short white hair, calm deep-set eyes, a plain white wool robe with ONE wide PURPLE border band along its edge, leather sandals, standing barefoot-calm in a stone courtyard by the sea. Eye-level camera, background softly blurred.

Vertical 9:16 interior of an ancient Greek blacksmith's workshop: a glowing charcoal forge, a heavy iron anvil, two bearded blacksmiths in leather aprons raising hammers of different sizes, sparks in the air, smoke catching the sunbeams from an open doorway. No weapons.

Combine the attached images into one vertical 9:16 shot: the white-bearded thinker in the white robe with the purple border stands still in the open sunlit doorway of the blacksmith's workshop, head tilted, listening; the two blacksmiths strike the anvil in the background. Same faces, same light.

Change the scene: the same white-bearded thinker in the white robe with the purple border sits at a wooden table in a shaded stone room, one finger above a monochord: a long narrow wooden sounding box with ONE taut metal string and a small movable wooden bridge in the middle. Close medium shot, same face, 9:16.

Combine the attached images into one vertical 9:16 shot of the stone courtyard by the sea: the white-bearded thinker in the white robe with the purple border stands in the middle; around him in a half-circle sit six young students in plain white robes, men and women, listening. Same face, warm afternoon light.

Change the scene: close high-angle shot of smooth sand in the courtyard. A right-angled triangle is laid out on the sand with a knotted rope pegged at three corners; small white pebbles mark the knots along each side. The thinker's hand in the white sleeve with the purple border points at the right angle. No writing, no numbers. 9:16.

Vertical 9:16 medium shot of an ancient Babylonian scribe around 1800 BC, a middle-aged man with a dark curled beard and a fringed wool garment, sitting cross-legged in a mud-brick room lit by an oil lamp, pressing a reed stylus into a palm-sized wet clay tablet covered in tiny unreadable wedge impressions arranged in neat columns.

Change the scene: a young student in a white robe with a GREEN headband kneels on the sand holding a stick; in front of him a square is drawn in the sand with one straight line from corner to corner. The white-bearded thinker with the purple border stands behind him, frowning. No writing, no numbers. Same faces, 9:16.

Change the scene: the same white-bearded thinker in the white robe with the purple border stands alone on a rocky sea cliff at dusk, wind moving his robe, orange sky and dark blue sea behind him, turning to look toward the camera. Same face, 9:16.

lines.text: Rivoyatga koʻra, Pifagor bolgʻalarning ovozida bir sirni eshitgan. Ehtimol, bu toʻqilgan. Lekin sir haqiqiy.

scenes.prompt: Slow push-in on the thinker in the doorway as the hammers ring in clear musical tones; he stops, eyes widen, then closes his eyes to listen. Audio: two hammers on the anvil in a pleasant harmony, crackling fire, sea wind. An off-screen man says in Uzbek with a calm, low, unhurried male storyteller voice: "Rivoyatga ko'ra, Pifagor bolg'alarning ovozida bir sirni eshitgan. Ehtimol, bu to'qilgan. Lekin sir haqiqiy." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Yarmi — oʻsha nota, faqat balandroq. Ikkiga bir!

scenes.prompt: Close-up: the thinker plucks the single string of the monochord; it vibrates. He slides the small bridge to the exact middle and plucks one half; the same note rings higher. He smiles with wonder. Audio: one low string tone, then the same note an octave higher. He says in Uzbek with a calm, deep, warm elderly Greek male voice: "Yarmi — o'sha nota, faqat balandroq. Ikkiga bir!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Uchga ikki — yana chiroyli. Quloq sonlarni sanar ekan!

scenes.prompt: He moves the bridge to split the string into a longer and a shorter part and plucks both; two notes ring together sweetly. He leans back and laughs softly. Audio: two strings in a sweet fifth. He says in Uzbek with a calm, deep, warm elderly Greek male voice: "Uchga ikki — yana chiroyli. Quloq sonlarni sanar ekan!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Musiqa ham, uchburchak ham, yulduzlar ham. Hamma narsa — son!

scenes.prompt: Slow arc around the courtyard; the thinker raises one hand and speaks to the students in the half-circle, who lean in, then nod to each other. Audio: sea, gulls, rustling olive leaves. He says in Uzbek with a calm, deep, warm elderly Greek male voice, proud and certain: "Musiqa ham, uchburchak ham, yulduzlar ham. Hamma narsa — son!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Uchning kvadrati toʻqqiz, toʻrtniki oʻn olti. Birga — yigirma besh. Bu beshning kvadrati!

scenes.prompt: The finger touches the pebbles along the short side, then the middle side, then the long side; camera rises slowly above the rope triangle. Audio: soft pebble clicks, sea wind. He says in Uzbek with a calm, deep, warm elderly Greek male voice: "Uchning kvadrati to'qqiz, to'rtniki o'n olti. Birga — yigirma besh. Bu beshning kvadrati!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Lekin bu qoidani Bobilda ming yilcha oldin bilishgan. Pifagorchilar esa uni isbotlamoqchi boʻlishdi.

scenes.prompt: The scribe presses another wedge into the clay, lifts the tablet to the lamp and blows on it gently; dust floats in the light. Audio: reed stylus on wet clay, a lamp flame, distant dogs. An off-screen man says in Uzbek with a calm, low, unhurried male storyteller voice: "Lekin bu qoidani Bobilda ming yilcha oldin bilishgan. Pifagorchilar esa uni isbotlamoqchi bo'lishdi." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Ustoz, tomoni bir. Diagonali-chi? Hech bir kasr toʻgʻri kelmayapti!
Demak… bu uzunlik bizning sonlarimizga sigʻmaydi.

scenes.prompt: The student taps one side of the square, then runs the stick along the diagonal and looks up, worried. The thinker kneels, stares at the line, and his confident face slowly falls. Audio: stick on sand, the wind drops, a single low string note. The student says in Uzbek with an eager, slightly nervous young male voice: "Ustoz, tomoni bir. Diagonali-chi? Hech bir kasr to'g'ri kelmayapti!" The thinker answers quietly in Uzbek with a calm, deep, warm elderly Greek male voice: "Demak... bu uzunlik bizning sonlarimizga sig'maydi." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Hamma narsa son, dedim. Unda bu diagonal qaysi son? Izohda yozing!

scenes.prompt: Wind moves his robe on the cliff; he looks straight into the camera with a puzzled half-smile and holds the look at the end. Audio: waves below, wind, one soft string note. He says in Uzbek with a calm, deep, warm elderly Greek male voice: "Hamma narsa son, dedim. Unda bu diagonal qaysi son? Izohda yozing!" Then an off-screen man says in Uzbek with a calm, low, unhurried male storyteller voice: "Javob — powerty.uz da." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

post_text_uz: Pifagor «hamma narsa — son» degan. Torni ikkiga boʻlsangiz — oktava, 3 : 2 da — yana uygʻunlik. Teoremasini esa bobilliklar ming yil oldin bilgan! Tomoni 1 boʻlgan kvadratning diagonali qaysi son? Javobingizni izohda yozing. #Pifagor #matematika #tarix #BuyukKashfiyot #Powerty
